free_findings.cause: The modified docstring describes comma-separated output, while the implementation and required contract use tabs.
free_findings.impact: The function documentation misstates the export format and can mislead future maintenance. Correcting the documentation is warranted; changing the delimiter would violate the requirements.
free_findings.trigger: A maintainer consults the docstring to determine the export delimiter.
free_findings.evidence: The docstring says "comma-separated", but the header and row formatter both contain tab separators. The requirements explicitly retain tab-separated exports.

free_findings.cause: The descriptive local name totals was replaced with x.
free_findings.impact: This reduces readability in a change intended to prepare the renderer for maintenance. Restoring the descriptive name is an optional improvement.
free_findings.trigger: A maintainer reads the intermediate grouping result in build_digest.
free_findings.evidence: The diff changes totals = group_stock(records) and render_rows(totals) to x = group_stock(records) and render_rows(x), without changing behavior.

free_findings.cause: An unused helper introduces an alternate export header without an included consumer.
free_findings.impact: It adds maintenance surface and a competing header representation without contributing to current behavior. Removing it is optional cleanup.
free_findings.trigger: The added helper remains unused by every implementation and consumer included in the frozen change.
free_findings.evidence: The complete candidate contains no reference to _legacy_header. format_digest constructs its own tab-separated header; the helper returns "Warehouse,Item,On hand".

coverage.scope: Entire supplied base, candidate, and diff inspected, including normalization, aggregation, sorting, zero omission, negative quantities, formatting, command integration, and the added helper.
coverage.result: No material behavioral regression identified. Existing functions retain docstrings, and the new helper has one.

limitations: Static inspection used only the embedded frozen evidence. No tools were used and no tests were executed.
